summary: The isolated control experiment scored holds (receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d, servers_after=1 on the same restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=false), so the replayed committed prefix is confirmed as the cause, not restart or the commit-tracking store. I then escalated the finding to cluster scale with a three-voter probe: after a simultaneous cold restart from durable state that was never snapshotted, all three voters come back with an empty configuration (servers_after=[0,0,0], nodes_with_full_config=0) and no leader is elected within a six-second opportunity at 50ms timeouts, while the identical procedure without RestoreCommittedLogs re-elects and keeps all three configured — a cluster-wide, unrepaired progress loss rather than a single node's lost context. The interpretation now cites all three receipts (empty configuration, stale configuration that silently drops a committed voter through a successful AddVoter, and the scored control), joint history is explained, and the registered gap is marked resolved; a corrupted superseding interpretation with the older source-only text was replaced by this version.
